January, 1996       Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 Tom Wilson...........03    05

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Dr. Tom Wilson, FALKIRK

Dear Ron,

I wonder if you can help me.  I
recently acquired a +D interface
(I already have the Disciple and
subscribe to OUTLET for it).  I
wanted to try the word processor
program in Issue 99 and put it
into my +D setup. I then SAVEd
the +D system file to Issue 99
and I think all I've done is to
corrupt it.

I enclose the disk for you to
check up on it and will be quite
willing to buy another if that
is what is needed.  In general
terms, however, I would like to
know - if I'm going to change


about between +D and Disciple -
whether in fact I will need TWO
separate disks:one with my Dis-
ciple's system file and another
with the +D one.

Another thing that is worrying
me is that I get error messages
like 106 when using OUTWRITE as
I'm doing now but don't kmow
what that means and I can't find
a table in the handbook to tell
me. I think it means there's not
enough room left on the disk
because the last time it happen-
ed, a fresh disk sorted it out.
But that was, as you will under-
stand, some time ago.
                Yours sincerely,

                 Dr. T. Wilson


Brian Cavers to Dr. Tom Wilson

Ron has sent you a replacement
disk and advised you that it is
OK to put both a Disciple and a
+D system file on the same disk.
I confirm this but would like to
add that many people do not seem
to realize that it's unnecessary
to put ANY system file on your
disks! If you want to boot up an
AUTO file then if you ALWAYS
make it the first file on a disk
then you need only enter LOAD P1
and can be sure it will load (as
you can with OUTLET). An ideal
candidate is a file menu loader
such as our CATLOADER. It's only
necessary to have ONE (and back-
up) of your disks with a system
file(s) on it.


Once you have booted up the sys-
tem DOS file you do not need to
do so again unless it gets corr-
upted.This does happen from time
to time and may not be detected.
Regular rebooting the DOS keeps
it refreshed,free of corruption.

However, even knowing that you
do not need to, many users still
PREFER to put the system file on
ALL disks so I have decided to
list all the pros and cons I can
think of - so at least everyone
knows what is what and can thus
decide accordingly. Of course,
a lot of effort may be needed to
move from one method to another!

Here's my list. Can you think of
any other relevant effects?...


           SYSTEM FILE ON DISKS:
                         ALL ONE
                         --- ---
Must put sys on disks.....Y   N
Waste space on ALL disks..Y   N
Dir entry wasted "   "  ..Y   N
Temporary POKE @ lost.....Y   N
Can only boot Drive 1.....Y   N
Longer loading time.......Y   N
MANY sysfiles if DOS mod..Y   N
Wrong DOS if alien disk...Y   N
More Keypresses to boot...N   Y
Must put AUTO only at P1..N   Y
DOS may remain corrupt....N   Y
DOS lost if reset.........N   N


On the SAM, the DOS is lost when
you reset so there is a greater
need to put the system on every
disk. Which leads me to...


OUTWRITE (on the SAM)  does give
most errors in full  (though it
may be that the earlier version
only gives the error number).The
later version would give...

  Error No.106 Directory full

As you guessed, the disk is full
effectively. However, if you get
MASTERDOS then you can have sub-
directories which the later ver-
sion of OUTWRITE supports and
then you can have far more than
just the 80 files per disk which
is the limit on SAMDOS.

                        Brian

From Chris Norfolk, HULL





Dear Ron + Brian,

I have now transferred a lot of
my OUTLET disks to 3.5" disks
via the external B drive on my
Plus 3.

The B drive is now working OK
but still, on various occasions,
does not want to obey the COPY
and CAT B commands. After much
frustration I have found the
answer - all it needs is a reset
of the Plus 3 and then it obeys
all the commands that I give it.


This problem may be why it app-
eared on the surplus market in
the first place but at least it
is now doing what it should do.
I did, at first, make a few mis-
takes on commands - but don't we
all when we get a new piece of
equipment.

I am thinking of getting a PC
IBM compatible as most radio
software today is far better
than the software I use for the
Spectrum. In most cases it is
the vast increase in speed that
produces far better results. It
so happens that a lot of suit-
able (and cheap) PD software is
now available. I shall now look
around but will not buy in a
hurry.


Best regards to all of the CHEZ-
RON TEAM

        Yours sincerely,

             Chris



Brian Cavers to Chris Norfolk

Thanks, Chris.

Next time that the +3 refuses to
obey the COPY or CAT B commands,
before you press RESET, place a
disk with some blank space on it
into the current drive and enter

SAVE "SYSVARS1.C"CODE 23296,438

Then press RESET and enter..

SAVE "SYSVARS2.C"CODE 23296,438

I'm just guessing that maybe a
system variable is confused and
will not let you use CAT B. By
comparing the two blocks of code
you can see what the differences
are.

If you do not know how to comp-
are the two blocks of code then
send them in to me and I will
have a look. Include a note to
remind me what it's all about!


There may well be several diff-
erences but if there is one that
is relevant it may be possible
to avoid the problem in the fut-
ure. Even if not, there may be
times when you have something
important in the machine and do
not want to reset. If a POKE can
restore the commands then it may
save the day without resetting
the machine.


Either way - I'm curious!


You've got me thinking now and
it does remind me that occasion-
ally my CATLOADER also fails to
recognize Drive B!  This is so
rare that I don't bother too
much about it but just reset. I
wonder if there is a DOS bug
that is common to all machines?

                      Brian

an A5 SAE and I will start to
make my new printer earn its
keep!


I also stock all types of utili-
ty and can supply software on
tape or +D 3.5"disc. Specific +3
programs can be supplied on 3"
disc but please note that I do
not supply demos on this format.

My address is:

          FOUNTAIN PD
         11 CAMEL ROAD
         LONDON E16 2DE


My entire demo collection is at
your disposal for future edit-
ions of OUTLET so please do not
hesitate to ask for any titles

as an OPENTYPE file for your

To finish, I have a couple of
questions concerning my printer.
I suffer from the dreaded '?' in
the left margin from Tasword 2.
Printer output from Tasword 128
+D version is fine.

Also, I cannot achieve a SAVE
SCREEN$2 dump using the +D,
though the SAVE SCREEN$ 1 comm-
and works fine. I have had a
look through the Epson manual

Any tips? The +D is very Epson

   Best wishes for the future

Brian Cavers to Dave Fountain

Thanks for the offer of PD and I
have sent you a blank disk and a
list!

The problem of the question mark
printing in Tasword 2 is a very
common one and, by coincidence,
another reader has also written
in this very month with the same
difficulty! The answer is in my
reply to Peter Angus elsewhere
in these OUTLETTERS.

Regarding the SAVE SCREEN$ 2 bug
the most likely cause is in the
DOS variables.These are the ones
you alter with POKE @ and there
is also a PEEK @ in OUTLET 71 to
show your current settings.


If you don't have OUTLET 71 it
doesn't matter because you can
still POKE @ the following to
see if it solves the problem.

The printer graphic codes for
SAVE SCREEN$ are @82 to @89. The
codes are included in the system
file you boot so they may vary
if you have different files that
you have saved at different
times after making changes or if
there has been any corruption.
You might try re-installing your
system file with MGT's original
set up program but I suspect the
problem may be that the type of
code used for graphics is not
used by your printer. My system
is set up to use ESC * which I
believe is the MGT default...


Check your printer manual. If it
does not include any reference
to ESC * (the codes are 27, 42)
then you will need to use others
such as ESC L.

To make things easier,I have put
a test program on the +D disk
version of OUTLET. It is not
linked to the CONTENTS page so
load it with LOAD d*"DUMPTEST".
It is not auto-run; just press
ENTER to list it. At the top is
line 100 with...

           LET C$="5"

This is, I believe, the default
MGT setting - so make sure your
printer is on-line and just run
the program to test it.


If it doesn't work,alter the "5"
in line 100 to "Y" and re-RUN.

Valid codes to insert into line
100 are "1" to "6"(probably will
not work if 5 does not as they
all use ESC *) or "K", "L", "Y"
and "Z" (MUST be capitals!). It
is interesting to try them all
to see the variations. If you
start the printout and don't
want to wait for the lot to
print and use BREAK then you may
need to switch your printer off
and on again to clear it else it
may not print properly next time
or may even give error beeps.

If one of the codes DOES work,it
is necessary to resave the DOS
file to make it permanent...


To resave your DOS system file,
to make any POKE @ changes perm-
anent(IE do this AFTER using any
POKE @'s and when you are happy
they are correct), do this...

            DISCIPLE...

   SAVE "SYSTEM" CODE 0,6656


      PLUS D WITH G+DOS...

 SAVE "+SYS 2a" CODE 8192,6656

Your +D system file may have a
slightly different name but I
think must always start with
"+SYS" or "+sys". I think the
Disciple one can be any name
beginning "SYS".


     PLUS D WITH BETADOS...

The system file has to be loaded
into high memory first. Copy the
system file to a spare disk with
our CATLOADER or...

    SAVE d*"+sysBETA" to d*

        ...then if anything goes
wrong you still have your origi-
nal system file.Add to DUMPTEST:

  50 LOAD "+sysBETA" CODE 40000
 300 SAVE "+sysBETA" CODE 40000,
     6850 : STOP

Alter the POKE @A,B in line 200
to...

        POKE 40000+A,B


Run the program and it should
alter and resave the system file
but I recommend you switch off
and reboot from that disk and
then test SAVE SCREEN$ 2 without
doing any POKE@'s to confirm it
is OK.

Although the BETADOS system file
is saved at the wrong address it
will still boot correctly BUT it
cannot be loaded with LOAD Pn
anymore (it will just load up to
400000). If anyone wants to know
how to correct this then let me
know.

If SAVE SCREEN$ 2 still does not
work no matter what POKE@'s you
use then let me know and tell me
the EXACT symptoms.


For example, does ANYTHING print
or does the Spectrum just 'hang'
or 'lock-up' or simply continue
to the next line?

The screen colours are converted
to black and white patterns when
printing. These patterns are
stored in @90 to @98 so if you
get a printout but it is just a
mess, ie, nearly all black or
almost all white then these may
be corrupt. They should be...

POKE @ 90, 43         91, 31
       92, 1          93, 7
       94,111         95, 7
       96, 1          97, 31
       98, 43

                        Brian

From Peter Angus, SWANSEA

Dear Ron,

Thanks for the sample and info
you sent(9th.December'94). I was
quite impressed but unfortunate-
ly can only be an occasional
subscriber.

On this disc you will find, or
have already found, my version
of Tasword 2, designated MP, ( =
Modified by Peter). The mods are
1. To slow the screens down imm-
ediately after saving a file, so
that there is time to read them.
2. To allow a choice, when load-
ing a file, on whether you wish
to view the catalogue, (instead
of having to).


I have a 48K Spectrum,originally
with rubber keys, but long since
fitted with a SAGA 1 Emperor
keyboard, which I like. It's a
pity they were not available for
very long. I use a Plus D disc
drive and Brother M1109 printer.

When printing from Tasword 2, I
have a couple of problems:-
a) There is a ? at the beginning
of each line. b) When in NLQ
mode, any ` sign is only printed
once, instead of twice, and is
therefore much lighter than the
rest of the text. Could you tell
me how to eliminate these prob-
lems please?
        Yours sincerely,

          Peter Angus

Brian Cavers to Peter Angus

Thanks for sending me a copy of
your Tasword setup which helped
me a lot to see how your system
has been configured.This is what
to do to remove those question
marks and get a NLQ pound sign..


1.Go to the Tasword 2 main menu
  and press BREAK to enter BASIC

2.Enter a new line...

  265 POKE @6,1:
      LPRINT CHR$ 27;"R";CHR$ 3;
      : REM UK - where # = `

  (the spacing isn't important
   but check every detail!)


3.Run the program and return to
  the main menu.

4.Select g for define graphics/
  printer.

5.Ignore the graphics but just
  press ENTER and you will see:
  Reset interface/printer codes?
  Press y for yes.

6.For interface control do ENTER
  four times to leave it as it
  is, ie, 0,0,0, 57855

7. Just press ENTER again to
   leave Printer carriage return
   =13

8. Enter 10 for printer linefeed
   (cures the question mark bug)


9.Just press ENTER again to
  leave the left margin at 8.

You should now resave the whole
program and code - in your case
by taking another snapshot. When
you want a pound sign you must
substitute a hash sign (#), eg,
for '`5.00' you would instead
type '#5.00'. The LPRINT CHR$ 27
;"R";CHR$ 3; in line 265 will
make your printer switch in the
printer's own pound sign in
place of the USA # sign.

An alternative,especially if you
want to be able to use both `
and # signs is to define one of
the graphics as character 156
which is a pound sign in the USA
printer's font! This is how...


1. Select g again at the menu.

2. Enter 142. This graphic is
   the block graphic which is
   roughly like a fat, blocky
   capital 'L' shape. Any other
   would do but since a ` sign
   is actually a fancy 'L'
   (remember the old L.S.D. for
   pounds, shillings and pence?)
   I thought it might be easier
   to remember.

3. Enter 156 then press ENTER
   once more to finish it. You
   should now see the graphics
   re-displayed with 156 to the
   right of the 142 line.

4. Press ENTER then N to get
   back to the menu.


5. BREAK and change the LPRINT
   CHR$ 27;"R";CHR$ 3; in line
   265 to...
   CHR$ 27;"R";CHR$ 0;:REM USA

Now, in the text editor, if you
want a # sign in the text you
can just type a # sign but if
you want a ` sign you need to
type graphic 142. To do this...

1. Press the graphic key (this
   is SHIFT with 9 on keyboards
   with no graphic key).

2. Press SHIFT with the '1' key
   to type the block graphic 'L'
   shape.

3. Press the graphic key again
   to get back to normal text.


Thus instead of `5.00,the screen
would show something like L5.00
(I can't use the graphic here in
OUTLET because we use it in our
text compression as a flag).

The POKE @6,1 enables the +D to
send printer codes but this will
disable LLIST so if you normally
prefer your printing to be in
'POKE @6,0' mode then insert the
POKE in line 290 thus...

290 RANDOMIZE USR 59806:POKE @6,
    0: GO TO 10

Remember to resave the program
to make permanent any changes. I
hope that helps.
                       Brian.

All good wishes for the New

          Yours truly,

          W.A. Yates


Brian Cavers to W.A. Yates

I can't remember what I said
before but pressing the RESET
button does the same as RUN USR
0 and is quicker and easier.

You should, by now,have received
your disk back. I have cured the
bug I think and saved a new copy
on your disk as 'folio3'. Thus..

Line 2515 changed to...
 LPRINT AT qpc,0;"Totals"; : LET
 b$=x$

Line 2525 deleted

Line 2535 changed to...
 LPRINT AT qpc,8+xpc;x$;AT qpc,
 17+xpc;b$


I don't think the program is PD
so we'd better not publish it. A
pity really as it is just the
sort of thing we like.

I don't have a copy of the Spec-
trum + manual but if you send a
photocopy of the printed listing
and a disk with the program as
typed in by you then I will have
a look at it to see why it will
not work. I assume you have
double-checked every dot and
comma???!!!

                          Brian

From J. Alan Sharvell, HARROW


Dear Brian & Ron,

Many thanks for the 100th edit-
ion of OUTLET which I am still
ploughng through at the moment
but, as I could not find the
DIGITAL TRACER in the OUTBOARD
section, I have decided to put
an ad in OUTBOARD myself which
may bring forth some sort of
info.

Sorry about the last letter en-
closing a letter to forward, re-
garding the dreaded disk prob-
lems since managing to locate
suppliers of new drive belts for
the +3. They are...


 SUPPLIERS OF +3 DRIVE BELTS...

        MR. A. J. HOWARD
         45 ALTYRE WAY
           BECKENHAM
              KENT
            BR3 3ED

  `2.45 inc pp & instructions

             OR...

          MR D. BARRET
         3 RUSSET CLOSE
           SCUANMORE
             SOTON
             HANTS
            SO23 2RU

       He SELLS +3 drives
        and may repair


I have fitted two to the +3s and
one to an Amstrad CPC 6128 all
of which are now behaving well.

One word of warning just in case

drops out and if not replaced

         Alan Sharvell


Brian Cavers to Alan Sharvell

Thanks,Alan. Those addresses are
very useful.I suspect that drive
belt slippage might be quite a
common fault on the +3. We have
two suspect machines and several
readers have written in with
what now sounds like it might be
belt slippage.

Ooops! I typed in four new OUT-
BOARD messages for David Wornham
last month- with numerous items.
I omitted ONE item - you guessed
it! The digital tracer!!! I've
now corrected this and you will
see it in David's OUTBOARD mess-
age - the one with white ink on
red paper.
                         Brian.

### Brian Cavers отвечает Dave Fountain

Что касается бага с `SAVE SCREEN$ 2`, то наиболее вероятная причина кроется в системных переменных DOS. Это те самые переменные, которые вы меняете через `POKE @`, а в OUTLET 71 также была программа `PEEK @`, показывающая ваши текущие настройки.

Если у вас нет OUTLET 71, это не беда, вы все равно можете попробовать применить следующие `POKE @`, чтобы проверить, решит ли это проблему.

Коды графики принтера для `SAVE SCREEN$` находятся по адресам от `@82` до `@89`. Эти коды содержатся в загружаемом системном файле, поэтому они могут отличаться, если у вас есть разные файлы, сохраненные в разное время после внесения изменений, или если произошел сбой. Моя система настроена на использование `ESC *`, что, как я полагаю, является умолчанием MGT...

Проверьте руководство к своему принтеру. Если в нем нет упоминания `ESC *` (коды 27, 42), вам придется использовать другие, например `ESC L`.

Чтобы облегчить задачу, я поместил тестовую программу на диск OUTLET для +D. Она не привязана к странице CONTENTS, поэтому загрузите ее командой `LOAD d*"DUMPTEST"`. Она без автозапуска; просто нажмите ENTER, чтобы вывести листинг. В самом верху находится строка 100 с:

```text
           LET C$="5"
```

Это, как я полагаю, стандартная настройка MGT — так что убедитесь, что принтер подключен и готов к работе, и просто запустите программу для проверки.

Если это не сработает, измените `"5"` в строке 100 на `"Y"` и запустите снова.

Допустимые коды для строки 100 — это от "1" до "6" (скорее всего, не сработают, если 5 не работает, так как все они используют ESC *) или "K", "L", "Y" и "Z" (ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО заглавные!). Если один из кодов СРАБОТАЕТ, необходимо перезаписать системный файл DOS, чтобы изменения вступили в силу насовсем...

Чтобы перезаписать системный файл DOS и сделать постоянными любые изменения через POKE @ (т. е. делайте это ПОСЛЕ использования POKE @ и когда убедитесь, что всё работает правильно), выполните следующее...

```text
 SAVE "+SYS 2a" CODE 8192,6656
```

Имя вашего системного файла +D может немного отличаться, но, полагаю, оно всегда должно начинаться с "+SYS" или "+sys". Системный файл Disciple, насколько я знаю, может иметь любое имя, начинающееся с "SYS".

```text

```

```text
    SAVE d*"+sysBETA" to d*
```

...тогда, если что-то пойдёт не так, у вас останется исходный системный файл. Добавьте в DUMPTEST:

```text
  50 LOAD "+sysBETA" CODE 40000
 300 SAVE "+sysBETA" CODE 40000, 6850 : STOP
```

Измените POKE @A,B в строке 200 на...

```text

```

Запустите программу, и она должна изменить и перезаписать системный файл, но я рекомендую выключить компьютер, перезагрузиться с этого диска и затем протестировать SAVE SCREEN$ 2 без каких-либо POKE@, чтобы убедиться, что всё в порядке.

```text

       92, 1          93, 7
       94,111         95, 7
       96, 1          97, 31
       98, 43
```

### Brian Cavers — Peter Angus

Спасибо за отправку копии вашей конфигурации Tasword, это очень помогло мне понять, как настроена ваша система. Вот что нужно сделать, чтобы убрать вопросительные знаки и получить знак фунта в качестве NLQ...

1. Зайдите в главное меню Tasword 2 и нажмите BREAK для выхода в BASIC.
2. Введите новую строку...

```text
  265 POKE @6,1: LPRINT CHR$ 27;"R";CHR$ 3; : REM UK - where # = `
```

(пробелы не имеют значения, но сверяйте каждую деталь!)

3. Запустите программу (RUN) и вернитесь в главное меню.
4. Выберите «g» для define graphics/printer.
5. Проигнорируйте графику, просто нажмите ENTER, и вы увидите: «Reset interface/printer codes?». Нажмите «y» (yes).
6. Для управления интерфейсом нажмите ENTER четыре раза, чтобы оставить всё как есть, то есть 0,0,0, 57855.
7. Просто снова нажмите ENTER, чтобы оставить «Printer carriage return = 13».
8. Введите 10 для «printer linefeed» (это устраняет ошибку со знаком вопроса).
9. Снова нажмите ENTER, оставив левое поле на 8.

Теперь вам следует перезаписать всю программу и код — в вашем случае сделав еще один snapshot. Когда вам понадобится знак фунта, вы должны использовать символ решетки (#), например, вместо «`5.00» вы печатаете «#5.00». Команда `LPRINT CHR$ 27;"R";CHR$ 3;` в строке 265 заставит принтер подставлять собственный встроенный знак фунта вместо американского знака #.

Альтернативный вариант, особенно если вы хотите использовать и знак `, и знак # — переопределить один из графических символов как символ с кодом 156, который является знаком фунта в американском шрифте принтера! Вот как это сделать...

1. Снова выберите «g» в меню.
2. Введите 142. Этот символ представляет собой блочную графику, похожую на толстую угловатую заглавную букву «L». Подойдет и любой другой, но поскольку знак ` — это, по сути, видоизмененная буква «L» (помните старое обозначение L.S.D. для фунтов, шиллингов и пенсов?), я подумал, что так будет проще запомнить.
3. Введите 156, затем нажмите ENTER еще раз для завершения. Теперь вы увидите заново отображенный список графики со значением 156 справа от строки 142.
4. Нажмите ENTER, затем N, чтобы вернуться в меню.
5. Нажмите BREAK и измените команду `LPRINT CHR$ 27;"R";CHR$ 3;` в строке 265 на...

```text
   CHR$ 27;"R";CHR$ 0;:REM USA
```

Теперь в текстовом редакторе, если вам нужен знак # в тексте, вы можете просто набрать #, а если нужен знак `, введите графический символ 142. Для этого:

1. Нажмите клавишу Graphics (на клавиатурах без нее — SHIFT + 9).
2. Нажмите SHIFT с клавишей '1', чтобы напечатать блочный графический символ в форме буквы 'L'.
3. Снова нажмите клавишу Graphics, чтобы вернуться к обычному тексту.

Таким образом, вместо `5.00 на экране будет отображаться что-то вроде L5.00 (я не могу отобразить этот символ здесь, в OUTLET, так как мы используем его в нашем алгоритме сжатия текста в качестве флага).

POKE @6,1 позволяет +D отправлять коды на принтер, но это отключит команду LLIST, поэтому, если вы обычно предпочитаете режим печати с 'POKE @6,0', вставьте этот POKE в строку 290 следующим образом:

```text
290 RANDOMIZE USR 59806:POKE @6, 0: GO TO 10
```

Не забудьте перезаписать программу, чтобы сохранить изменения. Надеюсь, это поможет.
